framework: WIDA English Language Development Standards Framework, 2020 Edition
disclaimer: EduWonderLab ACCESS Practice Lab is independent practice. It is not made, scored, endorsed, or validated by WIDA, and nothing here is an official ACCESS for ELLs task, score, or proficiency level.
supportVsLevel: Starting, Growing and Expanding in this lab are classroom support choices that a learner or teacher can change at any time. They are not WIDA proficiency levels and never become a label for a student.

matrix.task: Mr. Ortiz explains the rain garden
matrix.discourse: Follows an explanation organized by cause and effect and by sequence signals (First, Second, Finally).
matrix.sentence: Understands sentences that link a cause to a result (so, because).
matrix.word: Academic and topic words: runoff, absorb, filter, pavement.
matrix.evidence: Ordered four steps; inferred the speaker's purpose.
matrix.independent: Two plays, no transcript or frames, notes allowed, feedback only after Check.
matrix.supported: Replay by part, transcript after answering, Spanish word help.

matrix.task: Where Does the Rain Go? with Table 1 and a paired opinion
matrix.discourse: Reads a cause-and-effect explanation with a table and diagram, then a short argument.
matrix.sentence: Processes complex sentences with because, when, and noun phrases that pack details.
matrix.word: Infers runoff from context; reads cognates (absorb, filter).
matrix.evidence: Pinned the sentence that shows the cause; compared two table rows; connected two texts.
matrix.independent: No chunking, glosses, or hints until after Check.
matrix.supported: Chunked paragraphs, word help, cognate marks, read-aloud, evidence hint.

matrix.discourse: Produces a spoken explanation with a cause, a sequence, and a result.
matrix.sentence: Links ideas with because, so, first, then, finally.
matrix.word: Uses subject words from the picture: runoff, absorb, filter, pavement.
matrix.evidence: Recorded take, speaking time and pauses measured on the device, typed transcript analyzed for moves, self-check, teacher rubric option.
matrix.independent: Preparation timer, one prompt, no frames or model. A model answer is never offered before the learner speaks.
matrix.supported: Frames and a model answer appear only after a first take is recorded.

matrix.task: Argue for or against a school rain garden
matrix.discourse: Writes a claim, reasons, source evidence and a counterpoint.
matrix.sentence: Combines ideas with because, however, so and although.
matrix.word: Precise topic words and evidence phrases (according to Table 1).
matrix.evidence: First draft and revision compared on claim, evidence, linking and word choice; learner reflection.
matrix.independent: No frames, bank, or model; feedback only after submitting.
matrix.supported: Frames, word bank, and a model paragraph after the first draft.

inventory.area: Support vs independent modes with a visible evidence label
Listening: replay limit, notes, ordering, inference, transcript after answer
Reading: illustrated text, table, evidence pinning, paired text
Speaking: recorder, speech measures, self-check, re-record and compare
Writing: rule-based feedback, revision, draft comparison, reflection
Existing Speaking Studio, Writing Studio, Reading Room, missions, worlds
Practice tests and practice composite with labelled limits
Passport, share code, teacher evidence, family experience (EN/ES)
